Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). No Pool name and no live holding sits here (the Pool's sector relative-strength floor keeps telecoms out), so the Lists are unmoved this week. One notch, not two, because the base rate of 113 past group cases in this position has 55% back above the 200-day average within 26 weeks with a median of +2%, and no lower low has printed. Back to C on Industry relative strength above 30 by end-January with those results stable, or the ten-year under 4.5%; to F on a lower low, or churn and price cuts attributed to switching tools or satellites.

memo.verdict: Progress to Early-Stage. Bullish; medium conviction; the re-rating leg held as a working hypothesis until the September 2026 payout policy is seen. The park rule does not fire (management B; business quality C; predictability B on transmission; trackability C). The case clears the framework's 20% a year bar today on the eighteen-month path (modal 20.2% a year; entry at or below about EUR 21.2, which is today's price) and not on the three-year path (modal 15.4% a year; entry at or below about EUR 18.8, about GBP 16.0 at the block's price pair). Conditions named: the policy declared at about 70% of organic equity free cash flow and paid; the market moving from the earnings lens to the cash lens within two quarters of the policy; revenue holding flat to slightly up against Digi. The record's own statement of what it is betting on: that a declared payout of about 70% of a growing equity free cash flow makes the market value Zegona on the cash it pays rather than on the earnings its amortisation hides, before Digi or the suppliers take the growth away.
case: - The thesis in the record's words: Zegona is a private-equity turnaround of Vodafone Spain in a listed wrapper, and the case is a cash case, not a business case. The first-order change has travelled the whole 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain and is in the price at 1806.0p; the return from here rests on a payout policy of about 70% of equity free cash flow, due in September 2026, persuading the market to value the shares on the cash they pay (9.1x 24-month-forward equity free cash flow, an 11% yield) rather than on the earnings that amortisation hides (a 24-month-forward P/E of 14.28x, above the peer median).

- The change is internal, executed and unusually broad. Eight of the framework's twelve internal forces are present and acted on within 26 months. The false-positive checks fire once, on selling crown jewels; the record places that in the case against rather than as evidence the forces are weak. Internal forces A; the framework's screen rule (three strong, or chief-executive change plus guidance increase) is passed by both routes.

- The external forces net to a mild headwind, so the input picture is strong but not clean. Competition D (Digi tightening the low end while the top tier, MasOrange with 77% of synergies delivered and Telefónica with 0.7% convergent churn, repriced together three times in 2026: January inflation rises of 3.9%, the June Netflix pass-through). Supply side D (towers, FibreCo fees, content, wages, Huawei; counter-moves Cellnex, Ericsson, fixed-rate power). The company's own cycle B; Spanish macro B; demand C (volume tailwind, price headwind; not a 'Demand Inflection' force); regulation C (a EUR 45m antenna-tax refund; spectrum concessions extended ten years at zero cost; a EUR 430m annual spectrum tax; the 5G high-risk vendor law as an unpriced tail); disruption C; consolidation optionality C (Telefónica talks stalled on price; management's own value GBP 25 to 40 a share; 83% to 86% combined mobile share would face regulators).
counter_case: - At Building Block 1, the risks research's verdict at full force: the case is a false friend. The EUR 1.8bn of FibreCo proceeds and the EUR 60m of interest savings produced a headline transformation that masks a retail business in structural decline. Revenue growth of 0.4% a year in the bear models against 1.2% to 1.8% for peers; 49% of EUR 504m of gross receivables beyond 180 days at March 2026; a EUR 1,514m bridge from EBITDAaL of EUR 1,325m to a statutory net loss of EUR 189m in FY26. A network sold to landlords whose fees escalate (EUR 110m a year by 2027) while the retail price is set by a challenger at EUR 5 to EUR 10 a month; a tower threat the experts say the company cannot execute ("logistically and economically unfeasible"; EUR 250m of migration capex); a carry that gives two executives 15% of the upside; leverage that at 2.73x on a 3% revenue decline leaves the equity return "highly vulnerable". Once the cost and financial levers are spent, and the deceleration in EBITDAaL growth from +16.3% in Q4 FY26 to +2.5% in Q1 FY27 says they nearly are, the equity is a levered claim on a shrinking margin.

- What the record concedes there: the revenue line is the weakest in the sector set; earnings quality is poor and the cash bridge below operating free cash flow is not disclosed; the network sale capped the long-run margin and handed leverage to suppliers; the carry is expensive and the governance below standard; the deceleration is real; on the framework's default P/E footing the shares show no return, which is why the case rests on a metric choice the record has had to argue. Where the case against wins: if the policy disappoints or the market keeps the earnings lens, the return is 5% to 9% a year, not a loss; if Digi also breaks the ARPU line, it is the adverse drop-through and a loss.
triggers: - The payout policy (committed for September 2026; not in the research as of 16 September 2026). Alarm: materially below 70% of organic equity free cash flow. Invalidate: below 60% of equity free cash flow, or buybacks deferred beyond Q4 FY27.

- The market's lens after the policy. Alarm: policy declared and the multiple unchanged after one quarter. Invalidate: policy declared and the multiple not moved within two quarters, which the record says would mean the market has chosen the earnings lens.
- The cost programme. Alarm: EBITDAaL margin below 35% in a quarter; H1 FY27 operating free cash flow below EUR 400m. Invalidate: EBITDAaL margin sustained below 35%.

- Revenue against Digi. Alarm: service revenue growth below +1.0% in one quarter; Digi quarterly net additions above 150k; Digi ARPU declines worse than -5% at Q4 2026. Invalidate: service revenue growth below +1.0% for two consecutive quarters, or fixed broadband net additions beyond -10k a quarter. Confirm: Digi net additions moderating below 150k; Digi ARPU stabilising above -5% by Q4 2026; further front-book increases by Telefónica or MasOrange.
- Digi beyond the low end. Alarm: a Digi IPO revival or funding round. Invalidate: a 3% revenue decline flowing through at 70%.

- Vantage and supplier leverage. Alarm: a formal Vantage refusal without a Cellnex expansion announcement by mid-2027. The modal path carries a partial discount of 20% to 30% (EUR 30m to 45m a year from FY30, carried at EUR 35m), not the EUR 60m.
